Example: if doubling mesh cells changes pressure drop from 120 Pa to 118 Pa, the change is (120−118)/120 × 100 = 1.7 percent, suggesting near independence for that quantity. CFD results are estimates: report assumptions, mesh, turbulence model and uncertainty, and check current standards.

keyPoints: CFD solves conservation of mass, momentum and energy; for incompressible flow ∇·u = 0 and the Navier-Stokes equation gives momentum.
The finite volume method discretises equations over cells and conserves mass and momentum.
Explicit time steps are limited by the Courant number C = uΔt/Δx, often near 1 for simple advection.
Boundary conditions, especially inlet, outlet and wall conditions, must match the physical problem.
RANS models average turbulence while LES resolves large eddies; both have limits.
Verification checks the numerical solution, validation checks against experiment, and CFD results are estimates with uncertainty.

en.title: Advanced thermodynamics and heat transfer
en.short: Exergy, irreversibility, advanced convection and radiation, phase change and energy system optimisation.

sections.heading: Exergy and irreversibility
sections.text:
Exergy is the maximum useful work as a system reaches equilibrium with its environment at T0 and p0. For a steady-flow stream, specific exergy is ψ = (h − h0) − T0(s − s0). The exergy of heat Q at temperature T is (1 − T0/T)Q. Irreversibility is lost work: I = T0Sgen.

Example: 100 kW of heat crosses from 500 K to 300 K surroundings. Sgen = 100/300 − 100/500 = 0.1333 kW/K, so I = 300 × 0.1333 = 40 kW.

sections.heading: Advanced convection
sections.text:
Convection correlations use Nu = hL/k, Re = ρVL/μ and Pr = μcp/k. Forced convection often follows Nu = C Re^m Pr^n, with C, m and n set by geometry and flow regime. Dittus-Boelter for turbulent flow in a smooth tube is Nu = 0.023 Re^0.8 Pr^n, with n = 0.4 for heating and 0.3 for cooling. Natural convection uses Ra = Gr Pr and Nu = C Ra^n.

Phase change gives high heat transfer: boiling has nucleate, transition and film regimes; condensation may be filmwise or dropwise.

sections.heading: Radiation and phase change
sections.text:
Thermal radiation from a real surface is E = εσT⁴, where ε is emissivity and σ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant. View factors satisfy reciprocity A1F12 = A2F21. Radiation networks combine surface resistance (1 − ε)/(εA) and space resistance 1/(A1F12). Kirchhoff’s law states ε = α at the same temperature and wavelength.

Phase change releases or absorbs latent heat; heat exchanger design uses LMTD and effectiveness-NTU methods.

sections.heading: Optimisation and applications
sections.text:
Exergy efficiency is product exergy divided by input exergy. Pinch analysis uses a chosen minimum temperature difference to find the minimum utility demand and the pinch point.

In power plants, irreversibility is largest in combustion and heat transfer; in refrigeration, the compressor and condenser dominate. Optimisation balances capital cost against operating cost and exergy destruction. Design codes differ by country; check current local standards.

keyPoints: Specific flow exergy is ψ = (h − h0) − T0(s − s0), and heat exergy is (1 − T0/T)Q.
Irreversibility is lost work, I = T0Sgen, where Sgen is entropy generation.
Convection correlations use Nu = hL/k, Re = ρVL/μ and Pr = μcp/k, often in the form Nu = C Re^m Pr^n.
Radiation from a real surface is E = εσT⁴, and view factors obey A1F12 = A2F21.
Exergy efficiency is product exergy divided by input exergy, and pinch analysis sets minimum utility demand.
Phase change heat transfer depends on latent heat and on the boiling or condensation regime.

en.title: Research methods in mechanical engineering
en.short: Planning, conducting and defending a master’s research project in mechanical engineering.

sections.heading: Design and review
sections.text: Research design links a question to evidence. State a clear aim, one or two answerable objectives, the variables and the study limits. The project must be feasible with the time, equipment and skills available. A literature review is a critical survey, not a list of papers. Search journals, standards and conference proceedings; record search terms and selection rules so the review can be repeated. Identify the gap your project addresses. Example: a student in Kano studies heat loss from a solar dryer. She fixes the dryer size, ambient conditions and measured temperatures before building it, and states in advance how results will be judged.

sections.heading: Methods and data
sections.text: Choose experimental work, computational work, or both. Experimental methods need calibration, repeatability and an uncertainty budget. Computational methods need a stated model, boundary conditions, mesh or time-step checks, and validation against independent data. Validation means comparing predictions with measurements or accepted benchmarks. Data analysis starts with cleaning and plotting. Report means, spread and uncertainty; use statistical tests only when their assumptions hold. Example: the solar dryer student calibrates thermocouples, repeats each run three times, and compares a simple model with measured outlet temperature. She reports differences, not just agreement.

sections.heading: Ethics and defence
sections.text: Research ethics covers honesty, safety and respect for people and the environment. Do not fabricate, falsify or plagiarise. Cite sources and keep raw data so others can check your work. Seek approval from your institution before involving human participants or hazardous equipment; data protection and safety rules differ by country, so check the current local requirements. Professional registration and ethics approval differ by country; in Nigeria, engineering registration is through COREN. A dissertation documents the aim, method, results, analysis and limits. The defence is an oral examination: explain your choices, defend your evidence and admit uncertainty. Prepare figures that stand alone and a short summary of what is new.

keyPoints: Research design links a clear question to feasible evidence and stated limits.
A literature review must be critical, repeatable and must identify the gap.
Experimental work needs calibration, repeatability and an uncertainty budget.
Computational work needs stated assumptions, checks and validation against independent data.
Data analysis reports means, spread and uncertainty; statistical tests require their assumptions.
Ethics requires honesty, data retention, approval and local compliance; the defence explains and defends choices.
